# `get_stack_info`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Return the stack image dimensions, or with info_type fit_header the stack header summary and save name.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / established (64-bit build; 32-bit build established) |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xe0670, GetStackInfo @0x191e50, GetStackFitHeader @0x191ef0 (64-bit build) |

Default branch: returns the current stack width and height. With info_type fit_header: copies the last stack header, replaces the stack count and target name, sets the total exposure to frame count times exposure, and returns fit_header, save_fit_header and base_name; this requires at least one stacked frame (else 267). Despite being a getter it is graded MUTATOR because the header path writes diagnostic logs and model memos; the naming step does not create directories or save files. In the 64-bit build, on a master device with the wide-camera view predicate satisfied and the master bit unset, the request can first be relayed to a slave before it is parsed (process type 1); the relay can forward the original request and reconnecting the slave can synchronise storage state, so the call is tier C there. The 32-bit build has no relay and is tier B (probable). Relayed slave replies and errors are unresolved. No handler timeout; underlying calls can block.

Side effects: Serialises cached dimensions or header data and writes diagnostic logging and memos; in the 64-bit build the optional relay path can reconnect a slave and synchronise its storage state. No image is saved.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"get_stack_info"`. [READ] |
| `params` | object | no | - | Optional parameters of get_stack_info. Only object-form params are read; any non-object value (arrays and scalars included) is treated as an empty object and returns the dimensions. Unknown keys are ignored. [READ] |
| `params.info_type` | string | no | absent (dimensions) | Case-sensitive selector. The exact value fit_header selects the header branch. Absent, null, non-string or any other string returns the dimensions. No bad-selector error exists. [READ] |

## Reply

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `jsonrpc` | string | no | - | (error) Added by the socket layer (reply object constructor), not the handler fragment. Normally present; absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply. Receivers MUST NOT require it. Fixed value `"2.0"`. [READ; also OBSERVED on the wire (2026-10-12)] |
| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (error) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). On replies it is added by the socket layer and is normally present; receivers MUST NOT require it on replies (absent on a stop_func relay-failure reply). On events it is always written by the event constructor. [READ; wire shape also OBSERVED (2026-10-12)] |
| `method` | string | if the request had an id and a string method (handler errors and 103), except a locally built stop_func relay failure | - | (error) The request method, echoed. Absent on dispatcher errors 100 and 200 and on a stop_func relay failure. [READ] |
| `error` | string | yes | - | (error) Message looked up from the code; unknown codes yield "fail to operate". [READ] |
| `code` | integer | yes | - | (error) Nonzero. A requested code of 0 is coerced to 207. [READ] |
| `id` | any | yes | - | (error) The request id echoed with its JSON type; null on dispatcher errors 100 and 200, where it is the only way to recognise the reply and cannot be matched to a request. [READ] |

## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 267 | info_type fit_header and the last stack frame count is below 1 | `no image` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

A generic stack-info failure would forward the thread-local code, but the 64-bit helper reports success on every ordinary path. Errors forwarded from a relayed slave are unresolved.

## Example

Request, dimensions:

```json
{"id":81,"method":"get_stack_info"}
```

Request, header:

```json
{"id":82,"method":"get_stack_info","params":{"info_type":"fit_header"}}
```

Reply, ok-dimensions:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_stack_info","result":{"width":1080,"height":1920},"code":0,"id":81}
```

Reply, ok-header:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_stack_info","code":0,"id":82,"result":{"fit_header":{"header_date":"2026-01-31 21:04:05","bayer_pat":"RGGB","creator":"ExampleCreator","size":[1080,1920],"img_type":1,"obj_name":"Example target","stack_num":12,"exp_sec":10,"tot_exp_sec":120,"eqmode":1,"is_wide":0},"save_fit_header":{"CREATOR":"ExampleCreator","PRODUCER":"ZWO","PROGRAM":"example-fw","GAIN":80,"XBINNING":1,"YBINNING":1,"STACKCNT":12,"EXPOSURE":10,"TOTALEXP":120,"OBJECT":"Example target"},"base_name":"Example_target_stack"}}
```

Reply, no-frames:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"get_stack_info","error":"no image","code":267,"id":83}
```
